precursor_clusters.name: Multi-Signal Resource Saturation
precursor_clusters.earliest_detection_window_description: ~8 hours (memory pressure visible at first available telemetry, but CPU/load spike data only available at incident time due to observability gap)
precursor_clusters.notes: Strong co-occurrence at incident time, but limited by 8-hour telemetry gap. Memory was already saturated at earliest reading; CPU+load spikes appear only in the incident snapshot itself. True early warning potential for CPU/load components is unknown.

precursor_clusters.name: Persistent Memory Saturation (Background State)
precursor_clusters.false_positive_rate_notes: Memory was at 97-99% throughout the ENTIRE 64-hour observation window, including all non-incident periods. High memory alone cannot distinguish pre-incident from normal operation.
precursor_clusters.notes: This pattern is a necessary but not sufficient condition. It represents a chronic state (Docker VM reserving 8GB of 16GB host RAM) rather than an acute precursor.

precursor_clusters.name: Process Count Gradual Drift
precursor_signals: process_count gradually increasing from 617→623→667→668 over hours
precursor_clusters.earliest_detection_window_description: Gradual increase over ~8 hours (617 at T-8h → 667 at incident time)
precursor_clusters.notes: Process count increased by ~50 between early telemetry and incident time. Could indicate cumulative resource accumulation. However, only 2 observation points available (early cluster at 13:36 and incident cluster at 21:49+).

precursor_clusters.name: Prior Incident Cascade
precursor_clusters.notes: INC-002 was classified as a scoring artifact (not a true anomaly). The prior incident triggered additional monitoring that re-evaluated the same underlying condition. This is not a true precursor pattern — it's the reflex system re-checking an already-known condition.

false_positive_analysis.methodology: Compared precursor signal presence during incident windows vs. non-incident windows across the 64-hour observation period

findings.verdict: UNRELIABLE — present throughout entire observation, cannot distinguish incident from normal
PROMISING but insufficient data (n=1 incident, n=3 early baseline readings all <9%)
PROMISING but insufficient data (n=1). Earlier readings at 1.29-1.34.
MODERATE — elevated after incident but also during stable post-incident period
UNRELIABLE — disk grew monotonically, stayed elevated in all post-growth windows

INC-001.earliest_actionable: UNKNOWN — no intermediate telemetry between T-8h and T-0
INC-001.earliest_specific: 0 seconds (CPU/load spike only visible in incident snapshot)
INC-001.notes: The 8-hour telemetry gap is the critical limitation. Memory saturation was chronic, so it provides a permanent warning but not a timely specific alert.

INC-002.notes: INC-002 was a false positive (scoring artifact). The earliest 'precursor' was the prior real incident triggering re-evaluation.

overall_precursor_detection_accuracy.methodology: Weighted average: (cluster reliability × incident coverage × 1-false_positive_rate) across all clusters, penalized for small sample size (n=2 incidents, 1 true positive) and observability gaps

breakdown.observability_notes: Only 15% of the pre-incident window had telemetry coverage due to 8-hour gap before INC-001

overall_precursor_detection_accuracy.confidence_notes: Sample size of 2 incidents (1 true, 1 scoring artifact) is insufficient for statistically meaningful precursor validation. Score reflects analytical potential, not proven detection capability.

recommendations.detail: The 8-hour gap between T-8h telemetry and INC-001 is the primary limitation. Continuous or 5-minute-interval telemetry would enable precursor detection for CPU/load spikes.
recommendations.expected_impact: Would likely increase detection accuracy from 0.35 to 0.60+

recommendations.detail: Single-metric thresholds (memory >97%) are unreliable due to chronic elevation. A composite score combining CPU deviation + load deviation + process count trend + memory pressure would have much lower false positive rates.
recommendations.expected_impact: Estimated false positive reduction from 92% to <30%

recommendations.detail: Process count drift from 617→667 (+8%) over 8 hours was a gradual signal. A rate-of-change detector (ΔN/Δt) could provide earlier warning than absolute thresholds.
recommendations.expected_impact: Potential 30-60 minute early warning for resource accumulation incidents

recommendations.detail: Docker Desktop VM reservation (8GB of 16GB) permanently inflates host memory_used_percent to >97%. Subtract Docker VM reservation from baseline to reduce false positives.
recommendations.expected_impact: Would eliminate the primary source of scoring artifacts

recommendations.detail: Circadian baseline shows hour-22 has different normal ranges than hour-13. Time-aware precursor detection would reduce false positives from daytime/nighttime variance.
recommendations.expected_impact: Improved specificity for time-of-day dependent anomalies

recommendations.recommendation: Accumulate more incident data before trusting precursor patterns
recommendations.detail: With only 2 incidents (1 true positive, 1 scoring artifact), statistical validation is impossible. Minimum ~10 true incidents needed for reliable precursor fingerprinting.
recommendations.expected_impact: Required for any production-grade precursor detection system
